commands: collect-circuits repeated with outputs phase10-release-collection-repeat, phase10-stable-collection-a, phase10-stable-collection-b
test_corpus(catalog=phase10-release-collection/catalog.json, output=phase10-stable-recheck, samples=2, timeout=30, ids=all 12 synthetic plus all 7 implementation-drift cases; 16 unique IDs)
limits_and_gaps: 30-second hard deadline per compiler/backend process; routing has its own configured 10-second budget. No circuit was thinned to meet a deadline.
84 conservative static expressions and six non-JSON/accessor/cyclic runtime snapshots remain explicitly unresolved; inventories catalog their locations.
All 245 circuits in the stabilized source inventory were exercised; two earlier circuits remain retained and tested, for 247 total.
Original controller classifications are preserved. Reviewed results only reclassify stored rejection diagnostics and close interrupted stage states; no PASS was added by review.
Latest evidence selects actual rechecks for 16 cases, not a fresh full-corpus run at one immutable implementation revision. Each latest case has two samples with stable implementation hashes.
25-component RC and 100-component resistor benchmarks passed earlier but failed the recheck; size capacity is budget/load-sensitive and must not be declared robust.
Memory is sampled Windows child-tree working set every 20ms, excluding the harness; brief peaks can be missed. Measurements reflect concurrent work, not an idle dedicated performance host.
Native LTspice, simulation and browser rendering are not part of this corpus run. PASS requires compiler, bridge, backend connectivity, required routing, export and independent serialized checks.
Direct-router fixtures are snapshot as source circuits and run through normal layout; this does not replay every original test placement, injected fault or assertion.
